name: page-ceiling
description:
An appliance that ignores `offset` and answers every request with the same full page. The walk's two exits are an empty page and a short page, and this shape produces neither, so it used to spin until the task timed out with nothing in the log to say why. CONFIG maxPages (200) backs the walk via pager(); reaching the ceiling raises with a message naming the label and the maxPages key, which is what log_contains pins -- an incomplete import is reported as an error rather than silently truncated. The one real device streamed on page 1 must still be present in the output.

The route matching offset=200000 exists ONLY as a terminator for a regression. Serving the stuck page with when_exhausted=repeat_last alone would make an uncapped walk run forever and fail this scenario by timing out rather than by failing an assertion; with the terminator, an uncapped walk stops one request later and fails on request_count, requests_absent and the missing log line instead.

Every page carries a full 1000 rows because a shorter page is exactly what ends the walk (the served page size is learned from the first response, and these pages all match it). The first row of page one is a real device so the scenario still proves rows are parsed and reported; every other row has no id and is skipped, which is what keeps the ids unique across 199 repeats of the same page.

check_determinism is off: the scenario already costs 200 requests and 200,000 skipped rows, and a second identical run would only re-assert an id happy already pins.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in happy: the id is the bare Device42 id with no appliance scope.
